name: Toyota Tundra
engine: 3.5L twin-turbo V6 (i-FORCE, V35A-FTS), 389 hp — i-FORCE MAX hybrid, 437 hp combined (the previous 2007–2021 generation used a 5.7L V8, 381 hp)
reliability: 7/10 — the third-gen Tundra is a huge leap in capability: a twin-turbo V6 that out-powers and out-tows the old 5.7L V8, a 10-speed automatic, and up to 12,000 lbs of towing. The catch is that it traded a legendarily bulletproof V8 for a brand-new, more complex engine, and Toyota issued a significant recall on some 2022–2023 trucks for machining debris in the V35A engine that could cause failure (affected engines were replaced). Well-sorted trucks have been fine, but the long-term record is younger and less proven than the old V8's. Have the engine recall confirmed complete and buy with records.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate–High (large truck) · Maintenance ~$600/yr · Fuel economy is competitive for a full-size but still truck-thirsty · Strong resale, in line with the Toyota truck reputation
popular_mods: All-terrain tires and a leveling kit — the standard first upgrades
A tonneau cover and bed liner/bed rack for utility and overlanding
A weight-distributing hitch and brake controller for serious towing
Skid plates and recovery gear on the off-road-focused TRD Pro
Honest take: the twin-turbo V6 already makes strong power — money is better spent on towing gear, tires, and protection than on chasing more output from a new engine
oil_interval: Per the Maintenance Minder (~5,000–7,500 miles; many owners run 5,000 on a turbo engine)

generations.2nd Gen (2007–2021 US): The 5.7L 3UR-FE V8 Tundra — 381 hp, 6-speed automatic, and a near-legendary reputation for durability (many well past 300k miles). Thirsty and dated late in its run, but about as bulletproof as full-size trucks get.
generations.3rd Gen (2022–present US): A ground-up TNGA-F redesign that dropped the V8 for a 389 hp twin-turbo V6 (or a 437 hp i-FORCE MAX hybrid), a 10-speed automatic, coil-spring rear suspension, and up to 12,000 lbs of towing. Far more capable and modern, but a newer, less-proven powertrain.
generations.Note: Some 2022–2023 trucks were recalled for potential engine failure from manufacturing debris — verify the recall is closed by VIN.

common_issues: 2022–2023 V35A engine recall for machining debris that could cause engine failure — affected engines were replaced; confirm it is closed by VIN
A brand-new twin-turbo V6 with a shorter track record than the old 5.7L V8 it replaced
Truck-typical fuel economy despite the smaller-displacement engine, especially when towing
Some early-build interior/infotainment quirks on 2022 trucks
The move from the proven V8 to a turbo V6 is a character and long-term-confidence change for buyers used to the old truck
maintenance_tips: Confirm the 2022–2023 engine recall is closed by VIN before buying — this is the single most important check
Change the 0W-20 synthetic oil on a shorter interval given the turbo engine
Service the 10-speed automatic, transfer case, and differential fluids on schedule, especially if you tow
Use a proper weight-distributing hitch and brake controller when towing near the limit
Keep up with cooling-system service — turbo engines run hot, and clean coolant matters
